Not every environment takes MPP: where it is off the answer is 503 `mpp_off`. A person can then buy credit from a Checkout link: `POST /api/credits/checkout {"amount_cents": 1000}` answers its `url`.

data.current_description: An app is a command a Linux computer keeps running under its own process manager (supervisord): started at boot, started again when it exits (by its restart policy), and back by itself after a reboot, a crash, a host reboot, a restore or a wake. A running computer is asked for each app's state (one command on the computer; never a wake). Any other computer, or any computer with live=0, is answered from the last state on file, with live: false. Answers { supported: false, services: [] } for a computer that cannot have apps (only Linux computers on Orgo's hosts can).
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves all apps configured on the specified computer along with their current state. Apps are commands managed by supervisord that automatically restart according to their restart policy and persist across reboots, crashes, and restores. For running computers, state is queried in real-time. For stopped computers or those with live=0, state is returned from the last known state with live: false. Returns an object with 'supported' (boolean) and 'services' array. Returns { supported: false, services: [] } if the computer cannot have apps (only Linux computers on Orgo's hosts support apps). Each service object includes name, command, state, and other configuration details.
